deviceBridge.stopAndRemove: Stop the bridge and remove it from that computer, with its printers and pairing:
deviceBridge.theseNeed: These need the bridge set up to start with the computer, which it does the first time you open it. If a command says the path can't be found, open the bridge app again.
deviceBridge.stopsOnPrinter: That stops the bridge on the printer and deletes it with its settings and pairing.
deviceBridge.uninstallExplain: That stops the bridge, stops it starting with the computer, and deletes it with its printers and pairing. If it says the path can't be found, the bridge was never set to start with that computer: closing its window stops it.
deviceBridge.startsWindows: when you sign in to Windows
deviceBridge.startsMac: when you log in to the Mac
deviceBridge.offlinePrinter: The bridge runs on the printer itself and isn't answering. Check the printer is on and online; the bridge starts with it. This page reconnects by itself.
deviceBridge.offlinePrinterMore: Still offline? Restart the printer. A Snapmaker U1 loses the bridge with a firmware update: connect to it over SSH and paste the install line from Add a printer, On the printer, again.
deviceBridge.notRunningOn: The bridge isn't running on its {{computer}}.
deviceBridge.startsCheckOn: It starts by itself {{when}}, so first check that computer is on and online.
deviceBridge.startsCheckSignedIn: It starts by itself {{when}}, so first check that computer is on, signed in and online.
deviceBridge.startAgain: Still offline? Start it again on that computer, in {{shell}}:
deviceBridge.startsBackground: That starts it in the background and sets it to start with the computer again.
deviceBridge.logSays: If it keeps stopping, its log says why:
deviceBridge.pathNotFound: If the command says the path can't be found, download the bridge again from Add a printer and open it.
deviceBridge.testNote: This test site sets up a test bridge on the test relay. It installs next to your everyday bridge without touching it, and only ever updates from the test relay. Remove it with the same steps, or with Remove bridge.
deviceBridge.testNoteRuns: This test site sets up a test bridge on the test relay, which runs {{runs}}. It installs next to your everyday bridge without touching it, and only ever updates from the test relay. Remove it with the same steps, or with Remove bridge.
deviceBridge.copyLink: Copy the link to this page
deviceBridge.didntOpen: This page didn't open by itself?
deviceBridge.didntOpenHelp: The bridge opens this page on its own computer. If that is a different computer, you can carry on there. Or copy the address of the page it opened (it ends with a long code after #pair=) and paste it here:
deviceBridge.notReady: The bridge app isn't available to download yet. Try again in a few minutes.
deviceBridge.pickPrinterHelp: The bridge opens this page by itself and looks for printers on your network. Choose yours, then click Add printer. That's it: from now on the bridge starts by itself whenever that computer is on.
deviceBridge.intro: A small free app called the bridge connects your printer to this site. You set it up once.
deviceBridge.whyBridgeLong: Your printer is on your home network, which websites can't reach on their own. The bridge runs on the printer itself or on a computer in your home that is usually switched on.
deviceBridge.whyBridgeShort: Your printer is on your home network, which websites can't reach on their own.
deviceBridge.onComputerNotPhone: Do this on that computer, not on this phone.
deviceBridge.inDownloads: You'll find it in your Downloads folder.
deviceBridge.smartScreen: If a blue box says "Windows protected your PC", click More info, then Run anyway. Windows says this about new apps it doesn't know yet.
deviceBridge.pasteTerminal: Paste it into Terminal and press Return
deviceBridge.openTerminal: To open Terminal, press ⌘ Command + Space, type Terminal and press Return. Paste with ⌘ Command + V.
deviceBridge.macAllow: If your Mac asks whether the bridge may find devices on your local network, click Allow.
deviceBridge.pasteLinux: Paste it into a terminal on that computer and press Enter
deviceBridge.piNoScreen: On a Raspberry Pi without a screen, connect to it over SSH first. With no screen, the bridge prints a link instead of opening this page: open that link on any computer or phone.
deviceBridge.sshStep: Connect to the printer over SSH
deviceBridge.sshHow: From a terminal on your computer: <c>ssh root@{{addr}}</c>. Klipper printers on a Raspberry Pi use the Pi's own user instead of root.
deviceBridge.sshPasswords: Snapmaker U1: first turn on Settings, Maintenance, Root Access on the printer; the password is snapmaker. Creality K1: the password is creality_2023.
deviceBridge.pasteEnter: Paste this line and press Enter
deviceBridge.printerService: It installs the bridge on the printer as a service that starts with it and serves that printer. It updates itself, and it needs no computer left on.
deviceBridge.openLink: Open the link shown in the terminal
deviceBridge.openLinkHelp: Open it on this phone or computer; the printer is already on its list, so pick it and click Add printer. The link is also saved in Mainsail and Fluidd, in the config folder, as cloud-slicer-bridge-pairing.txt.
deviceBridge.u1Update: On a Snapmaker U1 a firmware update removes the bridge: paste the line again afterwards.
deviceBridge.macGatekeeper: Open the zip, then the app. The app isn't signed by Apple yet, so macOS stops it the first time: click Done, open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway. The Terminal line above avoids all of this.
deviceBridge.more: More about the bridge: is it safe, keeping it running, removing it
deviceBridge.keepRunning: Does it keep running? Yes. Once set up it starts by itself: on Windows and Mac when you log in (with no window: it runs in the background, out of the taskbar), on Linux and Raspberry Pi when the computer starts. The Device tab can reach your printer whenever that computer is on.
deviceBridge.addLater: Adding a printer later, or stopping it. Once the bridge is paired, add printers right in this dialog: search the network, or type an address. Or type the address here and run the command on the bridge's computer:
deviceBridge.restartsItself: The bridge restarts by itself to use a printer you add. It updates itself, and Printers & bridges offers an update when one is out.
deviceBridge.isSafe: Is it safe? The bridge only connects out to Cloud Slicer's relay, so nothing on your router is opened, and it only talks to the printers it found or you added. Your printer's API key is kept on that computer (one typed here goes straight to the bridge). The pairing link works like a password: anyone who has it can control your printers, so don't share it.
deviceBridge.thenPasteCode: then paste this setup code when it asks:
deviceBridge.runWhere: Run the bridge on a computer that stays on at home, on the same network as the printer, or on the printer itself.
deviceBridge.onComputerCopy: Do this on that computer, not on this phone: copy the command and run it there, or
deviceBridge.codeExpiredHelp: A setup code works for one hour. Here is a new one. If you already ran the command, paste this code where it asks; otherwise copy the new command.
deviceBridge.openPowershell: Press the Windows key, type PowerShell and press Enter. Paste the line with Ctrl + V (or a right-click) and press Enter.
deviceBridge.smartScreenShort: If a blue box says "Windows protected your PC" when you open it, click More info, then Run anyway.
deviceBridge.openTerminalAllow: To open Terminal, press ⌘ Command + Space, type Terminal and press Return. If your Mac asks whether the bridge may find devices on your local network, click Allow.
deviceBridge.macGatekeeperShort: Open the zip, then the app. It isn't signed by Apple yet, so the first time macOS stops it: click Done, open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway. The Terminal line avoids this.
deviceBridge.inLinuxTerminal: In a terminal on that computer
deviceBridge.piSsh: On a Raspberry Pi without a screen, connect to it over SSH first.
deviceBridge.inSsh: In an SSH window on the printer (Klipper printers)
deviceBridge.sshSetup: Connect first with ssh root@{{addr}}; Klipper printers on a Raspberry Pi use the Pi's own user instead of root. Snapmaker U1: turn on Settings, Maintenance, Root Access on the printer first; the password is snapmaker. Creality K1: the password is creality_2023. On a U1 a firmware update removes the bridge: make a new setup code and run the command again afterwards.
deviceBridge.setupCodeHelp: The setup code (also inside the commands) works once, for the next hour, and adds the bridge to your account.
deviceBridge.waitingHelp: This turns green by itself once the command has run.
deviceBridge.introAccount: A small free app called the bridge connects your printer to this site, and joins your Cloud Slicer account when you set it up.
